cells.location: Narasimgaṛh
cells.place: Inscription inside a cave-shelter on the top of a hillock adjacent to the village. Inside a cave about 100 metres away from the present temple of Hingalājadēvī. †
cells.remarks: Records the grant of lands to the Buddhist vihāra, (meaning the inscribed rock shelter itself). It also states that this and other rock shelters nearby were then traditionally known as having served as vihāra right form the days of Aśoka (Aśoka prākṛtikay-anuśruta-prākṛtana-śūnya -vihāreṣu, line 7), The lands granted to the vihāra were meant for the maintenance of the itinerant members of the bhikshu-samgha referred to as, āraṇya- kandādhyāyi. In characters of about the 7th century A.D.

cells.place: Tirumaṇḍanguḍi. Ruined Śiva temple. North, west and south walls.
cells.date: Regnal year 15, Ṛishabha ba. 12, Wednesday, Rēvati = 1231 A.D., April 30
cells.remarks: Slightly damaged. It appears that during the reign of Kulōttunga III the brāhmaṇa residents of Tirunaraiyūr-nāḍu in Kulōttungaśōḷa-vaḷanāḍu were exempted from the payment of certain taxes as well as rendering labour sevices to repair the embankment of the river Kāvēri. But during the reign of Rājarāja III, they were, probably imposed certain taxes and were also ordered to render services to the temple. They met at the temple and passed a resolution that they were liable to render only a few services. Many brāhmaṇa residents figure as signatories.
